name: La Reine Marlene - SIA Project 23 24
description:
Information Systems - academic year 23/24
Course Project
Scenario

La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of materials and products for the home. To improve the efficiency of its operations and the service to customers, the company is re-designing its information system. The details follow.

La Reine Marlene has a wide network of suppliers. The suppliers of La Reine Marlene will have to register in the system, providing their credentials and company details, including VAT number, address and the IBAN for payments. Registered suppliers can make proposals of their own products by entering in the system the following information for each product: category, sale price (the one that La Reine Marlene must pay to the supplier), availability, photo, description, guaranteed delivery time. The product categories are 16: Garden, Bathroom, Air Conditioning, Lighting, Decoration, Flooring, Doors and Windows, Carpentry, Kitchen, Storage, Tools, Electricity, Construction, Paints, Hardware, Furniture. Once a proposal has been entered, the supplier can no longer modify it until they receive a response notification.

When a supplier enters a proposal, the administration department of La Reine Marlene receives a message notifying the presence of a new proposal from the suppliers. At that point, it must verify the proposal and select one of the following options: Order accepted, Revisions requested, Order rejected. If the order is accepted, a separate order management process will start, to which the information on the price to be displayed in the store is added, so that this information will already be available in the subsequent processes. If instead revisions have been requested, they must be made explicit in a comment: at that point the supplier receives a notification and has 5 working days to modify the proposal, entering reply comments, and re-submit it. If the proposal has been modified within the 5 working days, then the proposal evaluation process restarts, otherwise the proposal is deleted from the system and the supplier notified. The administrators receive a reminder every 48 hours about the presence of a proposal that is waiting to be validated. A proposal that has not been verified within 10 working days is automatically rejected, and a specific message is sent to the supplier.

Once the products ordered from the suppliers are shipped and arrive at the destination La Reine Marlene site (there are dozens of them throughout Italy), they are entered in the inventory of all the products available in the store (La Reine Marlene has no warehouse: any available product is on display). Each product is catalogued according to its category, available quantity and location in the store. The location in the store is entered directly by the goods receiving staff: when an order is delivered, the staff members must verify each product. If there are no problems, the operator confirms the product and the system proposes a list of possible placements: the location is chosen, and the product is physically handed over to whoever will take care of its placement in the store and of printing the price to be displayed. Should there be problems with any product, the operator reports it by entering a comment and the product does not enter the store. At the end of these operations of verification of an order arrival, the operator closes the procedure and a new process starts, managed by the order department: if all the products have been accepted, the order is concluded and the payment sent. Otherwise, the order is updated and a new arrival that completes it is awaited. In both cases specific messages are sent to the supplier.

The system keeps track of stock in real time. An automatic notification is sent to the order department when a product reaches a critical reorder level (where it is specified). The administrators, in fact, can schedule automatic reordering and replenishment actions for specific products, in order to maintain an optimal inventory. In case of automatic reordering, a message is sent to the pre-established supplier, who has two working days to confirm acceptance of the order. In the absence of critical thresholds and of the related automation, the new order is managed by the order department with a separate process.

Customers looking for materials for the home can purchase the products both through the physical store and through the online store. In the online store, customers who have registered on the site can browse the digital catalogue, specify the desired products and quantities and complete the order. The system automatically calculates the order total, including taxes and shipping costs. Customers can choose among different payment options: credit card (Visa or Mastercard), Paypal, Satispay, the La Reine Marlene purchasing card, or immediate online bank transfer with the affiliated banks. Once the order is paid, the system keeps track of deliveries in real time. Customers receive a link by email through which they can follow the status of their shipments. In addition, those who have given consent to the use of the mobile phone number will receive notifications on updates to delivery times. Once the product arrives at its destination, the order is tracked as concluded. Deliveries are managed by partner companies, and each online purchase is randomly assigned to a shipping carrier. Consider that the online store is also accessible through a dedicated app: the operations and procedures are the same as those of the site.

La Reine Marlene offers a complete customer service through the information system. Customers can ask questions, request assistance or make complaints directly through the system. Support tickets are automatically assigned to a customer service agent. Every time a ticket is assigned, the agent receives a notification and has 24 hours to respond (if this does not happen, the ticket is reassigned to a new operator, and the statistics updated). The customer is informed upon receipt of the reply message, and has five working days to respond: otherwise, the ticket is considered closed.

Finally, the system collects data on orders, sales, inventory, customer support. These data are used to analyze performance and make strategic decisions.
highLevelGoals: Suppliers need to be able to easily and accurately submit proposals for their products, including all necessary details, to La Reine Marlene.
Suppliers require prompt notifications regarding the status of their product proposals (accepted, rejected, or revisions requested) to manage their business effectively.
Suppliers must have the ability to revise and resubmit their product proposals within a specified timeframe when revisions are requested by La Reine Marlene.
Suppliers need to be able to confirm acceptance of automatic reorders initiated by La Reine Marlene to ensure timely fulfillment.
The Administration Department Staff needs to quickly and effectively review and decide on supplier product proposals (accept, reject, or request revisions).
The Administration Department Staff must ensure that all supplier proposals are processed within defined timeframes to avoid automatic rejections and maintain operational efficiency.
The Administration Department Staff needs to be able to configure and manage automatic reordering and replenishment actions for specific products to maintain optimal inventory levels.
Goods Receiving Staff must be able to efficiently verify the accuracy and condition of delivered products against orders.
Goods Receiving Staff needs to be able to assign appropriate store locations for accepted products and facilitate their physical placement.
Goods Receiving Staff must have a clear mechanism to report any problems or discrepancies with delivered products to prevent them from entering inventory.
Order Department Staff needs to efficiently manage the conclusion of orders and initiate payments to suppliers once all products are accepted.
Order Department Staff must be able to manage and initiate new orders for products when stock levels reach critical reorder points or when automatic reordering is not configured.
Customers need to be able to browse a comprehensive digital catalogue and easily select desired products and quantities for purchase.
Customers must be able to securely complete their purchases through various payment options and receive accurate order totals.
Customers need to be able to monitor the status and progress of their shipments in real-time to anticipate product arrival.
Customers must be able to easily submit questions, requests for assistance, or complaints and receive timely responses from customer service agents.
Customer Service Agents need to be able to receive, manage, and respond to customer support tickets within specified timeframes.
Customer Service Agents aim to provide effective and satisfactory resolutions to customer issues to ensure a positive customer experience.
lowLevelGoals: The Supplier can submit a new product proposal including product name, description, category, unit price, and available quantity.
The Supplier can attach multiple images to a product proposal.
The Supplier can specify delivery terms and lead times for a product proposal.
The Supplier receives an email or in-app notification when the status of a submitted proposal changes (e.g., 'Accepted', 'Rejected', 'Revisions Requested').
The Supplier can view detailed feedback or reasons for a proposal's rejection or request for revisions.
The Supplier can retrieve a specific product proposal that has been marked for 'Revisions Requested'.
The Supplier can modify the product name, description, category, unit price, available quantity, images, and delivery terms of a retrieved proposal.
The Supplier can resubmit a modified product proposal for re-evaluation.
The Supplier receives a notification when an automatic reorder for their product is initiated by La Reine Marlene.
The Supplier can view the details of an automatic reorder, including product, quantity, and requested delivery date.
The Supplier can confirm their acceptance of an automatic reorder.
The Administration Department Staff can access a list of all pending supplier product proposals.
The Administration Department Staff can view the full details of a specific product proposal, including product information, images, and delivery terms.
The Administration Department Staff can mark a product proposal as 'Accepted'.
The Administration Department Staff can mark a product proposal as 'Rejected' and provide a reason.
The Administration Department Staff can mark a product proposal as 'Revisions Requested' and provide specific feedback for the supplier.
The Administration Department Staff can view the time elapsed since each proposal was submitted.
The Administration Department Staff can configure system-wide deadlines for proposal processing, after which proposals are automatically rejected.
The Administration Department Staff can configure automatic reordering for an accepted product, specifying reorder point, reorder quantity, and preferred supplier.
The Administration Department Staff can modify existing automatic reorder settings for any product.
The Administration Department Staff can view a schedule of upcoming automatic reorders.
The Goods Receiving Staff can scan the barcode of a delivered product to retrieve its order details.
The Goods Receiving Staff can input the received quantity and compare it against the ordered quantity for a product.
The Goods Receiving Staff can record the physical condition of delivered products (e.g., 'undamaged', 'damaged').
The Goods Receiving Staff can search for available store locations based on product category or size.
The Goods Receiving Staff can assign a specific store location to a verified incoming product.
The Goods Receiving Staff can print a label with the assigned store location for a product.
The Goods Receiving Staff can create a new report for product discrepancies, specifying the product, nature of the problem (e.g., 'damaged', 'incorrect quantity', 'wrong item'), and severity.
The Goods Receiving Staff can attach photos or other evidence to a discrepancy report.
The Goods Receiving Staff can submit a completed discrepancy report for review.
The Order Department Staff can mark an order as 'Complete' once all products have been verified and accepted by Goods Receiving.
The Order Department Staff can initiate payment to a supplier for a completed order.
The Order Department Staff can view the status of initiated payments to suppliers.
The Order Department Staff can view real-time stock levels for all products.
The Order Department Staff receives an alert when a product's stock level falls below its critical reorder point.
The Order Department Staff can manually create a new order for a product, specifying quantity and supplier.
The Customer can browse a digital catalogue of available products, filtered by category, price range, or other attributes.
The Customer can search for specific products by name or keyword.
The Customer can add a desired quantity of a product to their shopping cart.
The Customer can view the contents of their shopping cart, including product details, quantities, and subtotal.
The Customer can proceed from the shopping cart to the checkout process.
The Customer can select from various secure payment methods (e.g., credit card, PayPal, bank transfer).
The Customer can securely enter their payment details for the chosen method.
The Customer can view the accurate total cost of their order, including taxes and shipping fees, before confirming payment.
The Customer can confirm their order and initiate the payment process.
The Customer can access a list of their past and current orders.
The Customer can view the current status of a specific order (e.g., 'Processing', 'Shipped', 'Out for Delivery').
The Customer can view detailed tracking information for shipped orders, including carrier and tracking number.
The Customer can submit a new support ticket, specifying the type of inquiry (e.g., 'question', 'assistance request', 'complaint') and providing a detailed description.
The Customer can view the current status of their submitted support tickets.
The Customer receives a notification when a Customer Service Agent responds to their support ticket.
The Customer Service Agent can access a queue of all open customer support tickets.
The Customer Service Agent can assign an unassigned support ticket to themselves.
The Customer Service Agent can compose and send a response to a customer's support ticket.
The Customer Service Agent can mark a support ticket as 'Closed' once the issue is resolved.
The Customer Service Agent can access relevant customer information (e.g., order history, contact details) when handling a ticket.
The Customer Service Agent can offer various resolution options to the customer (e.g., refund, replacement, discount).
The Customer Service Agent can record the details of the resolution provided for a support ticket.
